content.text:
Probably not as a separate executable initially. Today it deserves a much stronger internal boundary, but I’d still keep `mise bootstrap` as the user-facing command.

The original command was only an orchestrator:

1. install system packages/files,
2. run `mise install`,
3. run the configured `bootstrap` task.

That was a natural mise feature, and the [original PR](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/10365) explicitly described it that way.

It has since grown into a distinct configuration-management subsystem:

- [`src/cli/bootstrap.rs`](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/24e9/mise/src/cli/bootstrap.rs:41) is 5,411 lines.
- It has 17 independently selectable phases.
- [`src/system/mod.rs`](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/24e9/mise/src/system/mod.rs:1) now covers accounts, files, packages, services, firewall, Compose, repos, dotfiles, remote execution, macOS defaults, launchd, systemd, secrets, history, and more.
- `src/system/` is roughly 81,500 of mise’s 353,000 Rust lines—although that includes package and history functionality used outside the aggregate bootstrap command.

How much does it reuse?

- Deep foundational reuse: mise configuration loading/composition, environments, templates, trust, variables, secrets, CLI/output infrastructure, and cross-platform utilities. Every bootstrap resource depends on this layer. Bootstrap-specific config composition is now wired directly into [`Config`](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/24e9/mise/src/config/mod.rs:411).
- Direct feature reuse: tool installation calls the ordinary `Install` implementation ([line 1829](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/24e9/mise/src/cli/bootstrap.rs:1829)); the final task uses the complete mise task runner ([line 2090](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/24e9/mise/src/cli/bootstrap.rs:2090)); status uses normal backend resolution and installation state ([line 4141](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/24e9/mise/src/cli/bootstrap.rs:4141)). Package and dotfile subcommands also reuse their respective command implementations.
- Mostly bootstrap-owned behavior: accounts, privileged files, services, firewall, Compose, remote orchestration, host defaults, launchd/systemd integration, convergence plans, and history/recovery.

So my rough characterization is:

- By phase count, only a small minority is “ordinary mise commands” reused wholesale.
- By architectural dependency, nearly everything depends on mise’s configuration and runtime semantics.
- By implementation volume, bootstrap has become a substantial product inside mise.

I would therefore split it into a `mise-bootstrap` internal crate—with a small interface to a `mise-core` config/tool/task layer—but continue shipping it in the single `mise` binary. There is currently only a binary target ([`Cargo.toml`](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/24e9/mise/Cargo.toml:55)), so making it a genuinely separate CLI now would require first turning mise internals into reusable libraries or resorting to subprocess calls.

A separate installed program would add a chicken-and-egg problem to a command whose main virtue is that downloading one `mise` binary can provision the rest of the machine. The code boundary is overdue; the executable boundary probably isn’t.
